# Grid-Scale Battery Storage Arbitrage in ERCOT (2024-2026)

## Summary

Merchant battery operators in ERCOT captured the widest energy-arbitrage
spreads of any US ISO across 2024-2025, driven by high solar penetration and
frequent scarcity pricing. This report sizes the revenue opportunity and the
main risks to it.

## Findings

Two-hour lithium-iron-phosphate systems earned an estimated $95-140 per
kW-year from energy arbitrage alone in 2024, before ancillary-service
stacking. Spreads narrowed through Q1 2026 as new capacity compressed the
evening net-load peak.

## Recommendation

Prioritise ERCOT West-zone interconnection queue positions at a two-to-four
hour duration; longer durations do not yet clear the arbitrage-only hurdle
rate at current spreads.

## Evidence appendix

- ERCOT 2024 State of the Market Report, Potomac Economics
- Modo Energy ERCOT benchmark, revenue-per-MW dataset (2024-2025)
- EIA Form 860M capacity additions, January 2026

## Limitations and data gaps

Revenue figures are backward-looking and exclude 2026 forward-curve risk.
Ancillary-service co-optimisation is modelled at a fixed 20% uplift; actual
stacking varies by operator. No primary operator interviews were conducted.
